test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 31 July, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in

Its corresponding direct speech.

She asked whether I was going to attend the seminar.

options.text: She asked, "Are you going to attend the seminar?"
She said, "You going to the seminar?"
She asked, "Will you be attending the seminar?"
She said, "Have you gone to the seminar?"

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She asked whether I was going to attend the seminar.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"whether I was going" becomes "Are you going"**
 
 
• Indirect question "whether I was going" is converted to direct question "Are you going."
 
• Pronoun "I" is changed to "you" to match direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "She asked"
 
• Converted to: "She asked" in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "Are" and ends with a question mark "?".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“**She asked, "Are you going to attend the seminar?*"*."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "She said, 'You going to the seminar?'" 

 
 
• Missing auxiliary verb "Are" makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She asked, 'Will you be attending the seminar?'" 
 
 
• Verb "Will you be attending" changes the tense and meaning from the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said, 'Have you gone to the seminar?'" 
 
 
• Changes tense and meaning, referring to a completed action instead of a future plan.
